Algebra I · Lesson 7.3

Slope

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Where a line is and how steep it is are two different questions, and 7.2 answered only the first. Steepness is a comparison of two changes, how much yy changes from one point of a line to another and how much xx changes between the same two points. Both are subtractions of coordinates, so any two points are enough to make the comparison.

Problem
A line passes through (2,5)(2,5) and (6,17)(6,17). Going from the first point to the second, find how much yy changes and how much xx changes, then enter the value of the change in yy divided by the change in xx.
Show a hint
  • Each change is a subtraction, the second point's coordinate minus the first point's. For yy that is 17−517−5.
  • The change in yy is 1212 and the change in xx is 6−26−2. Divide the first by the second.
Show the full solution
The change in yy is 17−5=1217−5=12 and the change in xx is 6−2=46−2=4, so the quotient is 124=3412​=3​. A quotient of 33 means yy changes by 33 for every 11 that xx changes.
Problem
Three more points are claimed to lie on that same line, (−1,−4)(−1,−4), (5,14)(5,14) and (9,25)(9,25). From (2,5)(2,5) to each of them, compute the change in yy divided by the change in xx. Two of the three quotients come out 33, the value from the previous problem, and one does not. Enter the xx-coordinate of the point whose quotient is not 33.
Show a hint
  • Run the same two subtractions three times, always starting from (2,5)(2,5), and compare each quotient with 33.
  • From (2,5)(2,5) to (−1,−4)(−1,−4) both changes are negative, −9−9 and −3−3, and a negative divided by a negative is positive. Check the other two the same way.
Show the full solution
From (2,5)(2,5) the quotient to (−1,−4)(−1,−4) is −9−3=3−3−9​=3, the quotient to (5,14)(5,14) is 93=339​=3, and the quotient to (9,25)(9,25) is 207720​. Only the third differs from 33, so the xx-coordinate asked for is 99​. Two different second points on the line both give 33, so the quotient does not depend on which pair is used. The one point that gives something else is off the line.
Key idea
The slope of a line. For two points (x1,y1)(x1​,y1​) and (x2,y2)(x2​,y2​) of a line, the slope of that line is m=y2−y1x2−x1,m=x2​−x1​y2​−y1​​, the change in yy divided by the change in xx, and mm is the standard letter for it. Every pair of points of one line gives the same value, which is why three different pairs above all gave 33, and the pair that gave something else used a point off the line. A slope is a property of the whole line, so any two of its points are enough to compute it.
Problem
A line passes through (−4,9)(−4,9) and (2,−9)(2,−9). Enter its slope.
Show a hint
  • Take (−4,9)(−4,9) first in both subtractions. The change in yy is then −9−9−9−9.
  • The change in yy is −18−18 and the change in xx is 2−(−4)=62−(−4)=6.
Show the full solution
Taking (−4,9)(−4,9) first, m=−9−92−(−4)=−186=−3m=2−(−4)−9−9​=6−18​=−3​. Between these points yy decreases while xx increases, so the top of the fraction is negative, the bottom is positive, and the slope is negative.
Problem
A line passes through (3,−4)(3,−4) and (9,8)(9,8). A student writes −4−89−39−3−4−8​ and reports −2−2, subtracting the yy-values in one order and the xx-values in the other order. Enter the correct slope.
Show a hint
  • Both differences have to be taken in the same order, so pick one point to come first and use that point first on the top and on the bottom.
  • With (9,8)(9,8) first in both, the top is 8−(−4)8−(−4) and the bottom is 9−39−3.
Show the full solution
With (9,8)(9,8) first in both differences, m=8−(−4)9−3=126=2m=9−38−(−4)​=612​=2​. The student's −2−2 has the right size and the wrong sign, because only the top was reversed, and a reversed top is the negative of the correct top.
Key idea
Keep the same point first in both subtractions. Either of the two points may be written first, but the choice on the top and the choice on the bottom have to match. Taking the other point first reverses the sign of y2−y1y2​−y1​ and of x2−x1x2​−x1​ at once, and the two reversals cancel, so y2−y1x2−x1x2​−x1​y2​−y1​​ and y1−y2x1−x2x1​−x2​y1​−y2​​ are the same number. Mixing the two orders reverses the sign of just one of them, so the result is the negative of the slope. That is where −2−2 came from for a line of slope 22, the right size with the wrong sign.

Writing the left-hand point first makes the change in xx positive, since the other point has the larger xx. The sign of the quotient then depends only on the change in yy, positive when the right-hand point is higher and negative when it is lower. So the sign of a slope follows from where two points are, with no coordinates needed.

Problem
Points PP and QQ lie on the same line, with QQ to the right of PP and lower than PP. No coordinates are given, so no number can be computed for the slope of that line, but its sign can be named. Enter the word positive or negative.
Show a hint
  • Take PP first in both subtractions. QQ is to the right of PP, so the change in xx is positive.
  • QQ is lower than PP, so the change in yy is a negative number while the change in xx stays positive. Think about the sign of a fraction whose top and bottom have opposite signs.
Show the full solution
Taking PP first, the change in xx is positive because QQ is to the right, and the change in yy is negative because QQ is lower, so the slope is negativenegative​. Taking QQ first flips the sign of both changes, so the quotient is negative either way.
Problem
A line passes through (−6,−5)(−6,−5) and (10,7)(10,7). Enter its slope as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Take (−6,−5)(−6,−5) as the first point and subtract in that same order on the top and the bottom. Both differences involve subtracting a negative number.
  • The top and the bottom share a common factor, so the fraction you get first is not in lowest terms. Divide both by that factor.
Show the full solution
Taking (−6,−5)(−6,−5) first, m=7−(−5)10−(−6)=1216=34m=10−(−6)7−(−5)​=1612​=43​​. Both differences are positive because the second point is above and to the right of the first. Stopping at 12161612​ is the common miss, since the answer was asked for in lowest terms.
Key idea
The sign of mm gives the direction and ∣m∣∣m∣ gives the steepness. A line with m>0m>0 rises from left to right, a line with m<0m<0 falls from left to right, and m=0m=0 means every point of the line has the same yy, so the line is horizontal. The number ∣m∣∣m∣ is how much yy changes across one unit of change in xx, so ∣m∣=4∣m∣=4 is a change of four units and ∣m∣=14∣m∣=41​ is a change of a quarter of a unit. Steepness is measured by ∣m∣∣m∣ and not by mm, so a slope of −4−4 is steeper than a slope of 33.

Two kinds of line from 7.2 have not been put through the definition, the horizontal and the vertical. Every point of a horizontal line has the same yy and every point of a vertical line has the same xx, so one of the two changes is 00 in each case. A 00 on top and a 00 underneath are not the same, as the next two problems show.

Problem
From 7.2 the graph of y=6y=6 is a horizontal line, and (−8,6)(−8,6) and (15,6)(15,6) are two of its points. Enter its slope, or the word undefined if it has none.
Show a hint
  • The two points have the same second coordinate, so start with the change in yy.
  • The change in yy is 6−66−6 and the change in xx is 15−(−8)15−(−8). Work both out, then divide the change in yy by the change in xx.
Show the full solution
The change in yy is 6−6=06−6=0 and the change in xx is 15−(−8)=2315−(−8)=23, so m=023=0m=230​=0​. Zero divided by a nonzero number is 00, so every horizontal line has slope 00, however far apart its two points are.
Fun fact
Gaspard Monge set out descriptive geometry around 1795, pinning a solid object down by its projections onto two perpendicular planes. France kept it a military secret for years before it was taught at the Ecole Polytechnique.
Problem
From 7.2 the graph of x=−3x=−3 is a vertical line, and (−3,4)(−3,4) and (−3,−9)(−3,−9) are two of its points. Enter its slope, or the word undefined if it has none.
Show a hint
  • The two points have the same first coordinate, so look at the bottom of the fraction before the top.
  • The change in yy is −9−4=−13−9−4=−13 and the change in xx is −3−(−3)=0−3−(−3)=0. Ask what number multiplied by 00 gives −13−13.
Show the full solution
The change in yy is −9−4=−13−9−4=−13 and the change in xx is −3−(−3)=0−3−(−3)=0, so the slope would be −1300−13​, and division by zero has no value. The slope is undefinedundefined​. Answering 00 is the standard slip. A slope of 00 is a number and belongs to a horizontal line, while a vertical line has no slope at all.
Key idea
A vertical line has no slope, and that is not the same as a slope of 00. Two points of a vertical line have the same xx, so x2−x1=0x2​−x1​=0, and the quotient is a division by zero, which no number equals. The slope of such a line is undefined, meaning the line has no slope at all. Two points of a horizontal line have the same yy instead, so the top of the fraction is 00 and the bottom is not, and the quotient is the ordinary number 00. The zero is on top for a horizontal line and underneath for a vertical one, and only the second case has no answer.

A slope is one change divided by another, which is what a constant rate was in chapter 6. When xx is a time and yy is a measured amount, the slope is how much yy changes per one unit of xx, and its units are the units of yy over the units of xx. The next two problems ask for a rate from two readings, then the steeper of two lines.

Problem
A tank fills at a steady rate. At 66 minutes it holds 2323 liters and at 2020 minutes it holds 5858 liters. Liters plotted against minutes give a straight line. Enter the slope of that line, in liters per minute.
Show a hint
  • The change in yy is a number of liters and the change in xx is a number of minutes.
  • The tank gains 58−2358−23 liters over 20−620−6 minutes. Reduce the quotient.
Show the full solution
The change is 58−23=3558−23=35 liters over 20−6=1420−6=14 minutes, so m=3514=52m=1435​=25​​. The units of a slope are the units of yy over the units of xx, so this line's slope is 2.52.5 liters per minute.
Problem
Line gg passes through (1,2)(1,2) and (5,20)(5,20). Line hh passes through (−3,11)(−3,11) and (2,−14)(2,−14). One of the two lines is steeper than the other. Enter the slope of the steeper line.
Show a hint
  • Compute both slopes first. Which line is steeper depends on the size of each slope and not on its sign.
  • Line gg has slope 9229​, which is 4.54.5. Compare that with the size of the slope of line hh.
Show the full solution
Line gg has slope 20−25−1=184=925−120−2​=418​=29​ and line hh has slope −14−112−(−3)=−255=−52−(−3)−14−11​=5−25​=−5. Steepness is measured by ∣m∣∣m∣, and ∣−5∣=5∣−5∣=5 is greater than ∣92∣=4.5​29​​=4.5, so the steeper line has slope −5−5​. The steeper line here is the one with the smaller slope, since a negative slope can still be the larger in size.
Key idea
Three points are collinear exactly when the two slopes are equal. Points AA, BB and CC are collinear when one straight line contains all three. If they are, the slope from AA to BB and the slope from BB to CC are both the slope of that one line, so the two values are equal. Through BB there is only one line with a given slope, so if the two values are equal then AA and CC lie on that one line too. For (9,25)(9,25) earlier the two values were not equal. With one coordinate unknown, setting the two slopes equal gives a single equation in that letter.

The last two problems use the definition backwards. In each one the slope is fixed by other information and a missing coordinate is what the question asks for. Writing the slope condition down leaves one equation in one letter, which is chapter 4's work.

Problem
The points (−2,3)(−2,3), (4,k)(4,k) and (10,23)(10,23) are collinear, so one straight line passes through all three. Only the middle point has an unknown coordinate. Enter kk.
Show a hint
  • Two of the three points are fully known, so the slope of the line comes from those two alone.
  • That slope is 2012=531220​=35​, and (4,k)(4,k) is 66 to the right of (−2,3)(−2,3).
Show the full solution
The outer points give m=23−310−(−2)=2012=53m=10−(−2)23−3​=1220​=35​. From (−2,3)(−2,3) to (4,k)(4,k) the change in xx is 66, so the change in yy is 6⋅53=106⋅35​=10 and k=3+10=13k=3+10=13​. Checking the other pair, (4,13)(4,13) to (10,23)(10,23) gives 106=53610​=35​, the same slope.
Problem
Line uu passes through (−6,4)(−6,4) and (2,−8)(2,−8). Line vv passes through (3,−7)(3,−7) and (n,5)(n,5). Line vv is exactly as steep as line uu, and vv rises from left to right while uu falls. Enter nn.
Show a hint
  • Find uu's slope first. Equal steepness means the two slopes have the same size, and a line that rises has a positive slope.
  • Line uu has slope −32−23​, so vv has slope 3223​, and vv's change in yy is 5−(−7)5−(−7).
Show the full solution
Line uu has slope −8−42−(−6)=−128=−322−(−6)−8−4​=8−12​=−23​, so both slopes have size 3223​, and vv rises, so its slope is +32+23​. Then 5−(−7)n−3=12n−3=32n−35−(−7)​=n−312​=23​ gives 3(n−3)=243(n−3)=24, so n−3=8n−3=8 and n=11n=11​. Reusing −32−23​ for vv gives n=−5n=−5, a line falling just like uu.

Every slope here came from two points of a line already drawn. A slope can also be known first. Exactly one line passes through a given point with a given slope. Lesson 7.4, Finding the Equation of a Line, turns a point and a slope into that line's equation.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A line passes through (−1,−2)(−1,−2) and (3,18)(3,18). Enter its slope.
Show the solution
m=18−(−2)3−(−1)=204=5m=3−(−1)18−(−2)​=420​=5​. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding, so the numerator is 2020 and not 1616.
Practice
A line passes through (−5,13)(−5,13) and (1,−11)(1,−11). Enter its slope.
Show the solution
m=−11−131−(−5)=−246=−4m=1−(−5)−11−13​=6−24​=−4​. A negative slope means the line falls from left to right.
Practice
A line passes through (−5,−4)(−5,−4) and (7,4)(7,4). Enter its slope as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
m=4−(−4)7−(−5)=812=23m=7−(−5)4−(−4)​=128​=32​​. A slope is reported in lowest terms, so 812128​ is not the final form.
Practice
A line passes through (−2,5)(−2,5) and (6,−11)(6,−11). A student computes 5−(−11)6−(−2)6−(−2)5−(−11)​ and reports 22. Enter the correct slope.
Show the solution
Putting the second point first in both, m=−11−56−(−2)=−168=−2m=6−(−2)−11−5​=8−16​=−2​. Subtracting in opposite orders on the top and the bottom flips the sign, so the student's 22 has the right size and the wrong sign.
Practice
UU and VV are two points on a line, and UU is to the right of VV and higher than VV. Enter the word positive or negative for the sign of the slope of that line.
Show the solution
Taking VV first, both changes are positive, since UU is to the right of VV and above it, so the slope is positivepositive​. With UU first both changes are negative and the quotient is the same positive number.
Practice
Four lines are given by two points each, (5,−2)(5,−2) and (5,6)(5,6), then (−7,3)(−7,3) and (9,3)(9,3), then (2,−1)(2,−1) and (6,5)(6,5), then (−8,1)(−8,1) and (−8,−6)(−8,−6). Enter how many of the four have slope 00.
Show the solution
Only (−7,3)(−7,3) and (9,3)(9,3) share a yy-coordinate, giving 016=0160​=0, so the count is 11​. The first and fourth pairs share an xx-coordinate, so those lines are vertical and have no slope rather than slope 00, and the third pair gives 64=3246​=23​.
Practice
The line through (−6,w)(−6,w) and (11,−8)(11,−8) has slope 00. Enter ww.
Show the solution
The slope is −8−w11−(−6)=−8−w1711−(−6)−8−w​=17−8−w​, and a fraction equals 00 only when its numerator is 00, so −8−w=0−8−w=0 and w=−8w=−8​. The line is horizontal, and every point on a horizontal line has the same yy-coordinate.
Practice
The line through (c,4)(c,4) and (−7,19)(−7,19) has no slope. Enter cc.
Show the solution
The slope is undefined only when the two xx-coordinates are equal, so c=−7c=−7​. Both points then lie on the vertical line x=−7x=−7. The change in xx is 00, and division by 00 is undefined.
Practice
A candle burns down at a steady rate. After 99 minutes it is 2323 cm tall and after 2424 minutes it is 1717 cm tall. Height plotted against time gives a straight line. Enter its slope, in centimeters per minute, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
m=17−2324−9=−615=−25m=24−917−23​=15−6​=−52​​. The candle gets 0.40.4 cm shorter each minute, and the slope is negative because the height decreases as time passes.
Practice
A shipping firm charges by weight. An 88 kg parcel costs 3737 dollars and a 2020 kg parcel costs 6464 dollars. Cost plotted against weight gives a straight line. Enter the slope of that line, in dollars per kilogram, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
m=64−3720−8=2712=94m=20−864−37​=1227​=49​​. Each extra kilogram adds 2.252.25 dollars.
Practice
Four lines have slopes −52−25​, 125512​, −74−47​ and 8338​. Enter the slope of the least steep one.
Show the solution
The sizes are 52=2.525​=2.5, 125=2.4512​=2.4, 74=1.7547​=1.75 and 83≈2.6738​≈2.67, and the smallest is 7447​, so the least steep line has slope −74−47​​. The minus sign stays, since the question asks for the slope and not for its size.
Practice
Line gg passes through (0,0)(0,0) and (7,−24)(7,−24). Line hh passes through (1,−4)(1,−4) and (6,13)(6,13). Enter the slope of the steeper line.
Show the solution
Line gg has slope −24−07−0=−2477−0−24−0​=−724​ and line hh has slope 13−(−4)6−1=1756−113−(−4)​=517​. Steepness is measured by ∣m∣∣m∣, and 247=12035724​=35120​ is greater than 175=11935517​=35119​, so the steeper line is gg, with slope −247−724​​. Both sizes round to 3.43.4 at one decimal place, so a rounded check is not enough here.
Practice
A line has slope 77 and passes through (2,−5)(2,−5). Another of its points has xx-coordinate 88. Enter that point's yy-coordinate.
Show the solution
The change in xx is 8−2=68−2=6, and y−(−5)6=76y−(−5)​=7 gives y+5=42y+5=42, so y=37y=37​. Checking, (2,−5)(2,−5) to (8,37)(8,37) gives 426=7642​=7.
Practice
A line passes through (4,−11)(4,−11) and (4,6)(4,6). Enter its slope, or the word undefined if it has none.
Show the solution
Both points have xx-coordinate 44, so the change in xx is 4−4=04−4=0 and the slope would be 6−(−11)006−(−11)​, a division by zero, so the slope is undefinedundefined​. A vertical line has no slope at all, which is not the same as having slope 00, and that is the horizontal case.
Practice
The points (−7,9)(−7,9), (1,−7)(1,−7) and (r,−16)(r,−16) lie on one straight line. Enter rr.
Show the solution
The first two points give m=−7−91−(−7)=−168=−2m=1−(−7)−7−9​=8−16​=−2. From (1,−7)(1,−7) to (r,−16)(r,−16) the change in yy is −9−9, so −9r−1=−2r−1−9​=−2 gives r−1=92r−1=29​ and r=112r=211​​. The unknown here is an xx-coordinate, so it is in the denominator of the slope, which makes the last step a division rather than a multiplication.
Practice
The line through (−4,3)(−4,3) and (8,12)(8,12) is exactly as steep as the line through (2,6)(2,6) and (n,−3)(n,−3), and the second line falls from left to right. Enter nn.
Show the solution
The first line has slope 12−38−(−4)=912=348−(−4)12−3​=129​=43​, so the second slope has size 3443​, and since that line falls the second slope is −34−43​. Then −3−6n−2=−9n−2=−34n−2−3−6​=n−2−9​=−43​ gives 3(n−2)=363(n−2)=36, so n=14n=14​. Taking the second slope as +34+43​ instead gives n=−10n=−10, and that line rises from left to right.
Practice
The points (−9,2)(−9,2), (−9,7)(−9,7) and (c,15)(c,15) lie on one straight line. Enter cc.
Show the solution
The first two points both have xx-coordinate −9−9, so the line through them is the vertical line x=−9x=−9, and every point of that line has first coordinate −9−9, giving c=−9c=−9​. The change in xx from (−9,2)(−9,2) to (−9,7)(−9,7) is 00, so that slope is undefined and the equal-slopes check does not apply.
